record.original_question: Is it consistent that every countably compact subset of every countably tight space is closed? In particular, does this follow from the Proper Forcing Axiom?

evidence.quote: Question 15. Is it consistent that countably compact subsets of countably tight spaces are always closed? Does it follow from PFA?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is said to have countable tightness if for every $A \subseteq X$ and every $x \in \overline{A}$, there exists a countable subset $B \subseteq A$ with $x \in \overline{B}$. A subset $Y \subseteq X$ is countably compact if every infinite subset of $Y$ has an accumulation point in $Y$ (equivalently, every countable open cover of $Y$ by open subsets of $X$ has a finite subcover relative to $Y$, in the Hausdorff setting).

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that for every (Hausdorff) topological space $X$ of countable tightness, every countably compact subset $Y \subseteq X$ is closed in $X$? In particular, does the Proper Forcing Axiom (PFA) imply this statement?
artifact.status_search_result: A. Dow established that PFA implies countably compact subsets are closed in regular spaces with hereditary countable π-character—a strictly stronger hypothesis than countable tightness. The general statement (for all countably tight spaces) does not appear to be fully resolved under PFA in the available literature, so the question remains partially addressed rather than fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Countable π-character, countable compactness and PFA (A. Dow)
status_evidence.snippet: PFA implies that countably compact sets are closed in regular spaces with hereditary countable π-character.
status_evidence.claim: PFA gives the conclusion in a restricted (hereditary countable π-character) class, not for arbitrary countably tight spaces.

status_evidence.title: Compact C-closed spaces need not be sequential (A. Dow)
status_evidence.snippet: A space X is C-closed if every countably compact subset is closed; countably compact C-closed spaces have countable tightness.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the broader question for countably tight spaces is studied but not resolved in full generality.
